label: Law group itself
summary: The law group object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it as the argument of a treasury budget window function that reads the change in the budget total and the number of receivers for that law group. Going by its name and that use, it only returns the law group it is called on.

label: Strength comparison itself
summary: The military strength comparison object itself, for passing on or accessing it.
details: Going by its name, it hands back the object it is called on. Vanilla has no use of it on this type; functions of the same name on other types are used to pass a widget on as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Strength frame number
summary: A whole number that picks which frame of an image to show for the military strength comparison.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `frame` of an image in the declare war interaction, the war overview window and shared GUI components. Going by its name and that use, it chooses the frame of a multi-frame image; the game does not say how the number is worked out.

label: Strength ratio
summary: A decimal number giving the ratio between the two compared military strengths.
details: Vanilla passes it to two helper functions (a max-scaled and a max-other-scaled progress bar value, with the numbers 100 and 200 as further arguments) and uses the results as `layoutstretchfactor_horizontal` in the declare war interaction. The game does not say what the numbers mean. Going by its name, it is the ratio of the two sides.

label: Strength ratio description
summary: A text describing how the two compared military strengths relate.
details: Vanilla shows it as a tooltip in the war overview window and in shared GUI components. Going by its name, the tooltip describes the strength ratio.

label: Strength ratio name
summary: A short text naming how the two compared military strengths relate.
details: Vanilla shows it as visible text in a shared GUI component. Going by its name and use, it is a short label for the ratio, where the description function gives the longer tooltip text.

label: Target allies count
summary: The number of allies on the target's side of the strength comparison.
details: Vanilla shows it in a text line that begins with the game's allies concept link, in the strength comparison of the military view. Going by its name, the target is the other side compared with the viewer.

label: Target strength description
summary: A text describing the target's side of the strength comparison.
details: Going by its name and its return type, it is text about the target's strength. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Target total strength
summary: The total military strength of the target's side of the comparison, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it with a soldier icon and no decimals, in the military view's total strength line. Going by its name, the target is the other side compared with the viewer.

label: Viewer allies count
summary: The number of allies on the viewer's side of the strength comparison.
details: Going by its name and its return type, it is the counterpart of the target allies count. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Viewer strength description
summary: A text describing the viewer's side of the strength comparison.
details: Going by its name and its return type, it is the counterpart of the target description. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Viewer total strength
summary: The total military strength of the viewer's side of the comparison, as a number.
details: Going by its name and its return type, it is the counterpart of the target total. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Strength comparison itself
summary: The military strength comparison object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name, it returns the object it is called on. Same-named functions on other types, such as Character.Self, are used in vanilla texts as arguments to other functions. There is no vanilla use on this type.

label: Should show strength
summary: Whether the military strength comparison should be shown.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `visible` setting of a shared GUI component, so the comparison is only displayed when this is true.

label: Council task itself
summary: The potential council task object itself, for passing on or accessing it.
details: Going by its name, it hands back the object it is called on. Vanilla has no use of it on this type; functions of the same name on other types are used to pass a widget on as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Can select task
summary: Whether this council task can be chosen right now.
details: Vanilla uses it in the council window as the `enabled` setting of an entry and in `visible` conditions that pick which icon of a task is shown. Those conditions also check whether the liege's council or the top liege's council is being shown.

label: Cannot select reason
summary: A text explaining why this council task cannot be chosen.
details: Vanilla shows it as the `text` of a widget in the council window. Going by its name, the text gives the reason the task cannot be chosen.

label: Council position
summary: The council position this task belongs to.
details: The game lists it as a Promote function that returns a council position object, so more can be read from that. No vanilla line uses it on this type. One council window line uses a function of the same name after PotentialTaskLocationWindow.GetTaskType, as a data context; that is a hint only.

label: Council task type
summary: The kind of council task this is.
details: The game lists it as a Promote function that returns the task's task type object, so more can be read from that. Vanilla uses it to set a data context, to compare with the fabricate claim task, and to show the type's name.

label: Dummy task
summary: A stand-in task object for this potential task, used as a data context.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data context of a part of the council window. Going by its name, it is a placeholder task, not an active one.

label: Dummy or active task
summary: The task that is currently active if there is one, otherwise a stand-in task, used as a data context.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data context of a part of the council window. Going by its name, it falls back to the placeholder task when the task is not active.

label: Task asset
summary: The set of images and graphics belonging to this council task.
details: The game lists it as a Promote function that returns a task asset object. Vanilla reads the task's icon and glow textures from it in the council window.

label: Task effect text
summary: A text describing what this council task does.
details: It takes one argument, which the game does not describe. Vanilla has no use with an argument; a localization line calls a same-named function on the active council task without one and shows it under an Effects heading.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: An argument the game does not explain.

label: Task is active
summary: Whether this council task is the one currently being carried out.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide parts of the council window and to pick between two tooltip texts, one for an active task and one for a potential one.

label: Task is enabled
summary: Whether this council task is enabled.
details: Going by its name and its return type, it is a yes or no check on the task. Vanilla does not use it on this type, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Task is visible
summary: Whether this council task should be shown in the council window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `visible` setting of parts of the council window.

label: Select task type
summary: Selects this council task type.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from clicks in the council window. Going by its name, it makes this task type the chosen one.

label: Council task itself
summary: The potential council task object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name, it returns the object it is called on. Same-named functions on other types, such as Character.Self, are used in vanilla texts as arguments to other functions. There is no vanilla use on this type.

label: Unit info itself
summary: The unit info object itself, for passing on or accessing it.
details: Going by its name, it hands back the object it is called on. Vanilla has no use of it on this type; functions of the same name on other types are used to pass a widget on as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Unit ID
summary: A text with the unit's identifier.
details: Vanilla shows it as raw text in a debug window that watches the AI war coordinator.

label: Unit owner name
summary: A text with the name of the unit's owner.
details: Vanilla shows it as raw text in a debug window that watches the AI war coordinator.

label: Unit war name
summary: A text with the name of the war the unit belongs to.
details: Vanilla shows it as a tooltip in a debug window that watches the AI war coordinator. Going by its name, it is the war the unit takes part in.

label: Unit info is valid
summary: Whether the unit info still points to a real unit.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `visible` setting in a debug window that watches the AI war coordinator, so an entry is only shown when this is true. The exact meaning of valid is not documented.

label: Pan to unit
summary: Moves the map view to the unit.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a click in a debug window that watches the AI war coordinator. Going by its name, it centers the camera on the unit.

label: Unit info itself
summary: The unit info object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name, it returns the object it is called on. Same-named functions on other types, such as Character.Self, are used in vanilla texts as arguments to other functions. There is no vanilla use on this type.

label: Heightmap itself
summary: The heightmap object itself, for passing on or accessing it.
details: Going by its name, it hands back the object it is called on. It is in the engine's internal GUI category (internalclausewitzgui); vanilla has no use of it on this type. The game documents nothing more.

label: Heightmap memory
summary: The texture memory the heightmap needs, in megabytes, as a decimal number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the map editor's heightmap resolution panel as 'Texture memory required: … MB'. It is a tool for the map editor, not for the game itself.

label: Heightmap itself
summary: The heightmap object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name, it returns the object it is called on. Same-named functions on other types are used in vanilla texts as arguments to other functions. There is no vanilla use on this type.

label: Heightmap painter itself
summary: The heightmap painter object itself, for passing on or accessing it.
details: Going by its name, it hands back the object it is called on. It is in the engine's internal GUI category (internalclausewitzgui); vanilla has no use of it on this type. The game documents nothing more.

label: Smooth amount
summary: The heightmap painter's smoothing strength, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the 'Smooth amount' field of the map editor's heightmap painter, next to the 'Smooth terrain' brush. Typing into that field changes it through SetSmoothAmount.

label: Reload heightmap
summary: Reloads the heightmap in the map editor's heightmap painter.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from a button whose tooltip warns that reloading wipes the undo history. It is a tool for the map editor, not for the game itself.

label: Heightmap painter itself
summary: The heightmap painter object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name, it returns the object it is called on. Same-named functions on other types are used in vanilla texts as arguments to other functions. There is no vanilla use on this type.

label: Set smooth amount
summary: Sets the heightmap painter's smoothing strength from the text typed into its field.
details: It returns nothing and takes no argument. Vanilla runs it when the text of the 'Smooth amount' field in the map editor's heightmap painter changes, so it reads the value from that field.

label: Painter mode itself
summary: The heightmap painter mode object itself, for passing on or accessing it.
details: Going by its name, it hands back the object it is called on. It is in the engine's internal GUI category (internalclausewitzgui); vanilla has no use of it on this type. The game documents nothing more.

label: Painter mode selected
summary: Whether the heightmap painter is the map editor mode chosen right now.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of the 'Heightmap Painter' button in the map editor, so the button looks pressed while that mode is on.

label: Painter mode itself
summary: The heightmap painter mode object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name, it returns the object it is called on. Same-named functions on other types are used in vanilla texts as arguments to other functions. There is no vanilla use on this type.

label: Heightmap resolution itself
summary: The heightmap resolution object itself, for passing on or accessing it.
details: Going by its name, it hands back the object it is called on. It is in the engine's internal GUI category (internalclausewitzgui); vanilla has no use of it on this type. The game documents nothing more.

label: Clear selection
summary: Clears the selection of heightmap tiles in the map editor.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the 'Clr' button (tooltip 'Clear selection') of the heightmap resolution panel.

label: Decrease resolution
summary: Lowers the heightmap resolution in the map editor.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the '-' button (tooltip 'Decrease resolution') of the heightmap resolution panel.

label: Rectangle select on
summary: Whether rectangle selection of heightmap tiles is switched on in the map editor.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of the 'Rectangle select' box in the heightmap resolution panel.

label: Increase resolution
summary: Raises the heightmap resolution in the map editor.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the '+' button (tooltip 'Increase resolution') of the heightmap resolution panel.

label: Invert selection
summary: Inverts the selection of heightmap tiles in the map editor: selected tiles become unselected and the others selected.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the 'Inv' button (tooltip 'Invert selection') of the heightmap resolution panel.

label: Is 16-bit
summary: Whether the heightmap is to be stored as a 16-bit heightmap.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of the '16' button (tooltip 'Store as 16 bit heightmap') under 'Heightmap bit depth' in the map editor's heightmap resolution panel.

label: Is 8-bit
summary: Whether the heightmap is to be stored as an 8-bit heightmap.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of the '8' button (tooltip 'Store as 8 bit heightmap') under 'Heightmap bit depth' in the map editor's heightmap resolution panel.

label: Reload heightmap
summary: Reloads the heightmap from the map editor's heightmap resolution panel.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from a button whose tooltip warns that reloading wipes the undo history.

label: Select all tiles
summary: Selects all heightmap tiles in the map editor.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the 'All' button (tooltip 'Select all') of the heightmap resolution panel.

label: Selected tiles
summary: The number of heightmap tiles selected in the map editor, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the heightmap resolution panel as '… tiles selected'.

label: Heightmap resolution itself
summary: The heightmap resolution object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name, it returns the object it is called on. Same-named functions on other types are used in vanilla texts as arguments to other functions. There is no vanilla use on this type.

label: Set 16-bit
summary: Makes the map editor store the heightmap as a 16-bit heightmap.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the '16' button (tooltip 'Store as 16 bit heightmap') of the heightmap resolution panel; Is16Bit tells whether it is on.

label: Set 8-bit
summary: Makes the map editor store the heightmap as an 8-bit heightmap.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the '8' button (tooltip 'Store as 8 bit heightmap') of the heightmap resolution panel; Is8Bit tells whether it is on.

label: Herd leaderboard itself
summary: The herd leaderboard object itself, for passing on or accessing it.
details: Going by its name, it hands back the object it is called on. Vanilla has no use of it on this type; functions of the same name on other types are used to pass a widget on as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Close leaderboard
summary: Closes the herd leaderboard.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a click in the Great Steppe window.

label: Army composition
summary: The makeup of the army of one entry in the leaderboard list, used as a data context.
details: Vanilla passes a character list item to it and sets the result as the data context of a part of the Great Steppe window. Going by its name, the result describes the types of troops in that character's army.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The list entry to look at.
fields.values: a character list item, as vanilla passes `CharacterListItem.Self`

label: Entry sub-region
summary: The sub-region of one entry in the leaderboard list, used as a data context.
details: Vanilla passes a character list item to it and sets the result as the data context of a part of the Great Steppe window. The game does not say what a sub-region is here.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The list entry to look at.
fields.values: a character list item, as vanilla passes `CharacterListItem.Self`

label: Leaderboard is visible
summary: Whether the herd leaderboard is currently shown.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `visible` setting in the Great Steppe window.

label: Herd leaderboard itself
summary: The herd leaderboard object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name, it returns the object it is called on. Same-named functions on other types, such as Character.Self, are used in vanilla texts as arguments to other functions. There is no vanilla use on this type.

label: Toggle leaderboard
summary: Opens the herd leaderboard if it is closed, and closes it if it is open.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a click in the Great Steppe window. The open and close behavior comes from the function's name.

label: Troop details itself
summary: The hired troop detail view object itself, for passing on or accessing it.
details: Going by its name, it hands back the object it is called on. Vanilla has no use of it on this type; functions of the same name on other types are used to pass a widget on as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Close troop details
summary: Closes the hired troop detail window.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a click in the hired troops detail window.

label: Hired troop
summary: The hired troop that the detail window is about, used as a data context.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data context of the hired troops detail window. Going by its name, it is the troop the window shows, and the parts inside read from it.

label: Open troop assignment
summary: Opens the view where troops are assigned to a title.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a click in the hired troops detail window. The meaning comes from the function's name.

label: Troop details itself
summary: The hired troop detail view object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name, it returns the object it is called on. Same-named functions on other types are used in vanilla texts as arguments to other functions. There is no vanilla use on this type.

label: Hired troop itself
summary: The hired troop entry itself, for passing on or accessing it.
details: Going by its name, it hands back the object it is called on. Vanilla has no use of it on this type; functions of the same name on other types are used to pass a widget on as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Can be extended
summary: Whether the hiring of this troop can be extended.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `enabled` setting of the extend button in the hired troops detail window, the button that calls the extend function.

label: Can be hired
summary: Whether this troop can be hired.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `enabled` setting of the hire buttons and of the reassign button in the hired troops detail window.

label: Can be reassigned
summary: Whether this troop can be reassigned.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `visible` setting in the hired troops detail window and the military window, next to the administrative reassign cost. The game does not say to whom or what it is reassigned.

label: Extend hiring
summary: Extends the hiring of this troop.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a click on the extend button in the hired troops detail window.

label: Reassign cost
summary: A text with the cost of reassigning this administrative army.
details: Vanilla shows it after the word Cost in the hired troops view, and as text in the military window. The word administrative comes from the function's name.

label: Reassign cost tooltip
summary: A tooltip text explaining the cost of reassigning this administrative army.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the hired troops detail window and the military window.

label: Administrative title
summary: The title that this administrative army belongs to.
details: Vanilla reads the title's name from it for the headers 'Army of ...' and 'Location: ...' in the hired troops view, and uses it as a data context. It is also used to find the title's holder.

label: Commander traits
summary: The list of the commander's traits.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the hired troops detail window. Going by its name, the commander is the one leading this troop.

label: Troop composition
summary: The makeup of this troop, used as a data context.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data context of parts of the military window. Going by its name, it describes which kinds of soldiers the troop has.

label: Current soldiers
summary: The number of soldiers this troop has now.
details: Vanilla shows it as a soldier count in the hired troops list, followed by the word soldiers.

label: Extend info
summary: A text with information about extending the hiring of this troop.
details: Going by its name and its return type, it is a text next to the extend function. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Extend tooltip
summary: A tooltip text for the button that extends the hiring of this troop.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the hired troops detail window.

label: Hirable ruler cost
summary: A text with the cost of hiring this ruler's troops.
details: Vanilla shows it after the words 'Hire cost' in the hired troops view. The game also has a differently spelled function, GetHireableRulerCost, used in the military window.

label: Hirable ruler status
summary: A text with the status of a ruler whose troops can be hired.
details: Vanilla shows it in the hired troops view and in the mercenaries part of the military view. The game does not say which statuses exist.

label: Hire tooltip
summary: A tooltip text for the button that hires this troop.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip on hire buttons in the hired troops detail window.

label: Hireable ruler
summary: The ruler whose troops can be hired.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context and reads the ruler's capital location and short name from it in the hired troops view.

label: Hireable ruler cost
summary: A text with the cost of hiring this ruler's troops.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the military window. The game also has a differently spelled function, GetHirableRulerCost, used in the hired troops view. Both look alike by name.

label: Hired by
summary: The ruler who has hired this troop.
details: Vanilla reads the hirer's short name from it in a line that says the troop is hired by that ruler. It also checks whether the hirer is at war, in the military window.

label: Holy order
summary: The holy order this troop is.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context and reads the order's capital (as headquarters) and its cost text from it. It also checks whether the player is the order's patron.

label: Leased titles
summary: The list of titles leased to the holy order.
details: Vanilla counts the list and shows the count after the word Holdings in the hired troops view. Going by its name, the entries are titles leased to the holy order.

label: Holy order patron
summary: The patron of the holy order.
details: Vanilla shows the patron's name after the word Patron in the hired troops view.

label: Knight count
summary: The number of knights in this troop.
details: Vanilla shows it followed by the plural word for knights in the holder's culture, in the hired troops list.

label: Knights tooltip
summary: A tooltip text about the knights of this troop.
details: Going by its name and its return type, it is tooltip text about the knights. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Martial skill item
summary: The martial skill entry of this troop's commander, used as a data context.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data context of a part of the hired troops detail window. The game does not say whose martial skill it describes; going by the name, it is the commander's.

label: Mercenary company
summary: The mercenary company this troop is.
details: Vanilla reads from it the company's culture name, its home county (shown as capital), and its cost and hire duration text, in the hired troops view.

label: Troop name
summary: A text with the name of this hired troop.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the hired troops detail window.

label: Troop name, no tooltip
summary: A text with the name of this hired troop, without a hover tooltip.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the military window. Going by its name, it differs from the plain name function by leaving out the tooltip.

label: Regiments
summary: The list of regiments in this troop.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the hired troops detail window, and checks that the list has at most four entries to decide what to show.

label: Soldiers bar ratio
summary: A decimal number for filling the soldiers progress bar of this troop.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `value` of a progress bar in the hired troops detail window. Going by its name, it is the share of soldiers present.

label: Troop title
summary: The title this troop is tied to.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the hired troops detail window. It also reads the title's holder to get the plural word for knights in the holder's culture.

label: Total soldiers
summary: The total number of soldiers this troop can have.
details: Going by its name and its return type, it is the full size next to the current soldier count. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Hire troop
summary: Hires this troop.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from hire buttons in the hired troops detail window and the military window.

label: Is administrative army
summary: Whether this troop is an administrative army.
details: Vanilla uses it in the hired troops detail window to show or hide parts, often together with whether the player hired it.

label: Is empty
summary: Whether this troop entry is empty.
details: Vanilla uses it in the military window to show one part when it is empty and another when it is not. The game does not say what empty means for a troop.

label: Is hireable ruler
summary: Whether this troop is a ruler whose troops can be hired.
details: Vanilla uses it in the hired troops detail window, beside the holy order and mercenary company checks, to choose which part to show.

label: Is hired
summary: Whether this troop is currently hired.
details: Vanilla uses it in the military window and the hired troops detail window, often together with whether the hirer is at war or whether the player is the holy order's patron.

label: Is hired by player
summary: Whether the player has hired this troop.
details: Vanilla uses it in the hired troops detail window, mostly with the administrative army check.

label: Is holy order
summary: Whether this troop is a holy order.
details: Vanilla uses it in the army window and the hired troops detail window to choose which part to show.

label: Is mercenary company
summary: Whether this troop is a mercenary company.
details: Vanilla uses it in the army window and the hired troops detail window to choose which part to show.

label: Hired troop itself
summary: The hired troop entry itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name, it returns the object it is called on. Same-named functions on other types, such as Character.Self, are used in vanilla texts as arguments to other functions. There is no vanilla use on this type.

label: Hiring causes bankruptcy
summary: Whether hiring this ruler's troops would send the hirer into bankruptcy.
details: Vanilla picks between a bankruptcy tooltip text and a debt tooltip text with it, in the military window. The word is spelled 'Bankrupcy' in the function's name.

label: Hiring causes debt
summary: Whether hiring this ruler's troops would put the hirer into debt.
details: Vanilla uses it in the military window as `visible` for a warning and as `tooltip_visible`, so the warning and its tooltip show only when this is true.

label: Troop regiment itself
summary: The hired troop regiment itself, for passing on or accessing it.
details: Going by its name, it hands back the object it is called on. Vanilla has no use of it on this type; functions of the same name on other types are used to pass a widget on as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Current soldiers
summary: The number of soldiers this regiment has now.
details: Vanilla shows it as the soldier count of a regiment in the hired troops view.

label: Men-at-arms type
summary: The men-at-arms type of this regiment.
details: Vanilla reads its icon, and its horizontal image for the culture of the regiment's owner, to draw the regiment in the government administration window and the hired troops detail window.

label: Regiment bar ratio
summary: A decimal number for filling the progress bar of this regiment.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `value` of progress bars in the hired troops detail window. Going by its name, it is the share of soldiers present.

label: Regiment
summary: The regiment behind this hired troop entry.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context, and reads the regiment's owner and the owner's culture from it, in the government administration window and the hired troops detail window.

label: Total soldiers
summary: The total number of soldiers this regiment can have.
details: Going by its name and its return type, it is the full size next to the current soldier count. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Is levies
summary: Whether this regiment is levies.
details: Vanilla uses it in the government administration window and the hired troops detail window to show one part for levies and a different part when it is not. The game does not explain what levies means here.

label: Troop regiment itself
summary: The hired troop regiment itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name, it returns the object it is called on. Same-named functions on other types, such as Character.Self, are used in vanilla texts as arguments to other functions. There is no vanilla use on this type.

label: History entry itself
summary: The history entry itself, for passing on or accessing it.
details: Going by its name, it hands back the object it is called on. Vanilla has no use of it on this type; functions of the same name on other types are used to pass a widget on as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Actor
summary: The character who did what the history entry records.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the artifact details window, reads the actor's house from it, and compares it with the recipient. Going by its name, the actor is the one who acted, and the recipient the one acted on.

label: Date
summary: The date of an entry in an artifact's history.
details: Vanilla uses it in the artifact history texts (created, stolen, given …), turned into text with GetString, as the entry's heading. The game does not register its return type.

label: Description
summary: A text describing what the history entry records.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the artifact details window.

label: Location
summary: The place where an event in an artifact's history happened.
details: Vanilla uses it in the artifact history texts ('… at …', '… after the siege of …', '… in …') and shows its name with GetNameNoTooltip. The game does not register its return type.

label: Recipient
summary: The recipient of the history entry.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the artifact details window. It compares it with the actor and shows the recipient part only if the entry has a recipient that is not the same as the actor.

label: Holy site
summary: The holy site an artifact was enshrined at or removed from, in an entry of its history.
details: Vanilla shows its name in the artifact history texts 'Enshrined at the holy site of …' and 'Removed from the holy site of …'. The game does not register its return type.

label: Title text
summary: A text with the title of the history entry.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the artifact details window.

label: Type name
summary: A text with the type of the history entry.
details: Vanilla has no use on this type. Going by its name and its return type, it names the kind of event recorded. The game documents nothing more.

label: Has actor
summary: Whether the history entry has an actor.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `visible` setting in the artifact details window.

label: Has location
summary: Whether the history entry has a location.
details: Vanilla has no use on this type. A same-named check on another type is used to decide if a place name or a prompt to choose one is shown.

label: Has recipient
summary: Whether the history entry has a recipient.
details: Vanilla uses it in the artifact details window to decide whether to show the recipient part.

label: Has recipient holy site
summary: Whether the history entry has a holy site as recipient.
details: Going by its name, it is the check that goes with the recipient holy site. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: History entry itself
summary: The history entry itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name, it returns the object it is called on. Same-named functions on other types, such as Character.Self, are used in vanilla texts as arguments to other functions. There is no vanilla use on this type.

label: Holding itself
summary: The holding itself, for passing on or accessing it.
details: Going by its name, it hands back the object it is called on. Vanilla has no use of it on this type; functions of the same name on other types are used to pass a widget on as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Can construct a building
summary: Whether the given character can build at least one building in this holding.
details: Vanilla passes the player and uses it as the `visible` setting of a map icon. Going by its name, it is true if any building is available to build.

label: Barter goods income
summary: The amount of barter goods this holding brings in, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it next to the barter goods icon in the my realm window, and as a signed number in the ledger.

label: Barter goods tooltip
summary: A tooltip text explaining the barter goods income of this holding.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the county view and the my realm window.

label: Holding type under construction
summary: The type of holding that is being built here.
details: Vanilla uses it on this type in the holding view's texts for cancelling a construction, reading the type's name ("Abort ... Construction"). A contract event does the same on another type's holding. The game documents nothing more.

label: Building under construction
summary: The building that is being constructed in this holding.
details: The game marks it as a promote function: it turns the holding into the building object. Vanilla reads the building's name from it in the outliner.

label: Construction progress
summary: How far the construction in this holding has come, used as a progress bar value.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `value` of a progress bar in the outliner.

label: Construction time left
summary: How much time is left until the construction in this holding is done.
details: Vanilla uses it in the construction tooltip of the my realm window, on a holding reached as HoldingItem.GetHolding, and a contract event uses a same-named function on another type. The game does not say the unit or format of the time.

label: Garrison size
summary: The current size of this holding's garrison, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as the `text` of a map icon.

label: Current great building type
summary: The great building type this holding currently has.
details: Going by its name, it concerns great buildings. The game does not say what it returns when there is none. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Current special building type
summary: The special building type this holding currently has.
details: Going by its name, it concerns special buildings. The game does not say what it returns when there is none. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Duchy building type
summary: The duchy building type that belongs to this holding.
details: Going by its name, it concerns duchy buildings. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Great building type
summary: The great building type that belongs to this holding.
details: Going by its name, it concerns great buildings. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.
